newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two Osaka shinkin banks say to merge in October.
newsitem.headline: Two Osaka shinkin banks say to merge in October.

text.p: Two credit associations, known as "shinkin banks" based in Osaka, western Japan, said on Friday that they will merge on an equal basis as of October 6.
The two are Osaka Shinkin Bank and Sanwa Shinkin Bank.
Shinkin banks are larger than credit unions but are not classified as "banks" under Japanese financial laws.
They lend money mainly to members but take deposits widely. Most borrowers are small- and medium-sized businesses.
Unlike credit unions, they are monitored by the Finance Ministry.
Under the merger agreement, Osaka Shinkin Bank will be the surviving bank, they said in the statement.
The merger will create a shinkin bank with assets of 617.56 billion yen and loans of 455.3 billion yen. The number of branches at the merged shinkin bank will total 45.
